correctness.rationale: For each v in the faulted B columns, every face containing v can be enlarged by the surviving hub u; otherwise replacing u by v in a hypothetical new independent k-set contradicts the face condition. Therefore the link of v is a cone and sequential removals give a strong collapse. The simultaneous vertex retraction is contiguous to the identity, so respects the preserving symmetry subgroup. The remaining graph is exactly \(K_{s+1,b-t}\), whose face complex is the join of the two \((k-2)\)-simplex skeleta. The explicit acyclic skeleton matching gives integral wedges without torsion. Augmentation-lattice inclusions split, and exterior powers/tensor products preserve split injectivity. A standard-library verifier reconstructed and checked all faces, dominations, GF(2) boundary ranks, and Euler characteristics at every deletion stage for four finite parameter triples (26 stages). Finite field calculations are only corroboration of the unbounded integral proof.

value.rationale: A complete structural classification for naturally nested multi-vertex rectangular edge faults on bicliques, with explicit integral homotopy, symmetry modules and all nonzero inclusion maps. It exposes an abrupt degree change after a contractible plateau: early \((2k-3)\)-dimensional classes disappear, while final faults create \((k-2)\)-dimensional classes. Unlike an arbitrary numerical special case this is an infinite three-parameter family with a canonical defect-collapse principle; the known complete-bipartite core is credited rather than presented as novel. The precise fault shape is a natural reliability operation, not an unmotivated slice.
